title: How to Scrape Daraz Product Data: Prices, Sellers and Stock (2026 Guide)
desc: Step-by-step guide to scraping Daraz products in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Myanmar. Export prices, discounts, sellers and stock to CSV or Excel without code.
answer: Open the Daraz Product Scraper on Apify, choose a country domain (bd, pk, lk, np or mm), add search keywords or category URLs, and press Start. Each product comes back with its price, discount, seller, rating, sold count and stock status, ready to export as CSV, Excel or JSON. It costs $1.00 per 1,000 products.
toc: What data you can get from Daraz
How to scrape Daraz in 5 steps
body:
Daraz is the largest online marketplace in South Asia, with storefronts in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Myanmar. If you sell on Daraz, supply brands that do, or research the market, product data from Daraz tells you who sells what, at what price, and how fast it moves.

Daraz has no public product API, so copying data by hand is the usual fallback. This guide shows how to collect it automatically with a ready-made scraper, without writing code.

What data you can get from Daraz

The Daraz Product Scraper reads Daraz search and category pages and returns one row per product:

GroupFields
Producttitle, description, productId, sku, brand, categoryIds
Pricingprice, originalPrice, discountPct, currency
SellersellerName, sellerId, location
Social proofrating, reviewCount, soldCount
StatusinStock, isSponsored, badges
LinksimageUrl, productUrl, country, scrapedAt

Prices come back in the local currency of each market: BDT, PKR, LKR, NPR or MMK.

How to scrape Daraz in 5 steps

  1. Open the scraper. Go to the Daraz Product Scraper on Apify and sign in with a free Apify account.
  2. Pick the market. Set country_domain to bd, pk, lk, np or mm.
  3. Add what to search. Enter keywords such as "earbuds" in search_keywords, or paste up to 100 category or search URLs in startUrls.
  4. Set filters and limits. Sort by popularity or price, set a minimum rating or a price range, and choose how many products or pages to collect.
  5. Run and export. Press Start. When the run finishes, download the results as CSV, Excel or JSON, or send them to Google Sheets.

Example input

This input collects up to 500 earbuds from Daraz Bangladesh, sorted by popularity, with a minimum 4-star rating:

{
  "country_domain": "bd",
  "search_keywords": ["earbuds"],
  "sortBy": "popularity",
  "minRating": 4,
  "maxProducts": 500
}

Tips for complete, clean results

  • Use category URLs for full coverage. Keyword searches return what Daraz ranks for that word. A category URL returns the whole category.
  • Keep out-of-stock items for research. includeOutOfStock is on by default, which shows you demand that sellers are not meeting.
  • Choose pages or products as the limit. maxPages is useful for quick samples. maxProducts is better when you need an exact row count. Set it to 0 for no limit.
  • Schedule it. A daily run turns one export into a price history you can chart.

How much it costs

The scraper charges $1.00 per 1,000 products. Collecting 10,000 products costs about $10, and Apify's free plan covers small test runs. Higher Apify plans get a discount on the per-result price.

Is scraping Daraz allowed?

The scraper collects product information that Daraz shows publicly to every visitor. You are responsible for how you use the data, so check Daraz's terms and local rules for your use case, and avoid collecting personal data you have no reason to hold.
faq: Can I scrape Daraz reviews too?
Yes, with the separate Daraz Product Review Scraper. The product scraper returns ratings and review counts, not review text.
Does it work with product detail pages?
No. Use search, category or catalog URLs. To collect data for specific products, search by the product name or use the review scraper with the product URL.
Can I get the data through an API?
Yes. Every run is available through the Apify API, and you can call the scraper from Python or JavaScript.

title: How to Export Daraz Product Reviews to CSV or Excel
desc: Export Daraz product reviews with ratings, review text, photos and votes to CSV or Excel. Filter by star rating and sort by most recent. Works in all 5 Daraz countries.
answer: Paste one or more Daraz product URLs into the Daraz Product Review Scraper on Apify, set the matching country (BD, PK, LK, MM or NP), choose a sort order and star filter, and run it. You get every review with its rating, text, date, photos and votes, exported to CSV, Excel or JSON for $1.00 per 1,000 reviews.
toc: How to export reviews step by step
What to do with the data
body:
Reviews are the most honest data on Daraz. They tell you what buyers like, what breaks, and what sellers promise but do not deliver. Reading them one page at a time on the site is slow, and Daraz offers no review export.

The Daraz Product Review Scraper collects them for you and puts every review in one spreadsheet.

Why export Daraz reviews

  • Product research: check what buyers complain about before you stock a product.
  • Quality control: pull every 1 and 2 star review for your own listings each week.
  • Competitor analysis: find the repeated complaints in rival products and fix them in yours.
  • Sentiment scoring: feed review text into an AI model or BI tool.

What each review includes

GroupFields
ReviewreviewID, reviewContent, rating, reviewTime, boughtDate
ReviewerreviewerID, reviewerName (as Daraz shows it)
Engagementlikes, upVotes, downVotes, replies
Mediaimages, videos
ProductproductID, productTitle, productUrl, skuInfo, sellerId, country

How to export reviews step by step

  1. Copy the URLs of the Daraz products you want to analyse.
  2. Open the Daraz Product Review Scraper on Apify and paste them into urls.
  3. Set country to the market that matches the URLs: BD for daraz.com.bd, PK for daraz.pk, LK for daraz.lk, NP for daraz.com.np, MM for shop.com.mm.
  4. Choose a sort order and, if you want, a star filter.
  5. Press Start, then export the dataset as CSV or Excel.

Sorting and star filters

SettingValuesUse it for
sorting_order0 relevance, 1 most recent, 2 rating high to low, 3 rating low to highUse 1 for weekly monitoring, so new reviews come first
star_filter0 all, or 1 to 5Use 1 or 2 to collect only complaints

This input collects only 1-star reviews from a product on Daraz Pakistan, newest first:

{
  "urls": ["https://www.daraz.pk/products/..."],
  "country": "PK",
  "sorting_order": 1,
  "star_filter": 1
}

What to do with the data

Start simple. In Excel or Google Sheets, count reviews by rating and by month to see if quality is improving. Then search the review text for words like "broken", "fake" or "late" to group complaints. For larger volumes, run the text through a sentiment model or ask an AI assistant to summarise the top five complaints.

To compare products, pair this export with the Daraz Product Scraper, which gives you price, sold count and seller for the same items.
faq: How much does it cost?
$1.00 per 1,000 reviews. A product with 2,000 reviews costs about $2 to export in full.
Are reviewer names shown in full?
Daraz masks most names on its own pages, and the scraper returns them the way Daraz shows them.
Can I export reviews for many products at once?
Yes. Paste as many product URLs as you need into one run. They must all be from the same country domain.

title: How to Export YouTube Comments to Excel or CSV (No API Key)
desc: Export all comments and replies from any YouTube video or Short to Excel, CSV or JSON. No YouTube API key or coding needed. Includes likes, reply counts and video stats.
answer: Paste up to 20 YouTube video or Shorts links into the YouTube Comments Scraper on Apify, choose Newest or Top, decide whether to include replies, and run it. You get every comment with its text, likes, reply count, author and the video's own stats, exportable to Excel or CSV. No API key is needed and it starts at $0.50 per 1,000 comments.
toc: The problem with the YouTube API
How to export comments in 4 steps
Data you get for each comment
body:
YouTube comments are unfiltered customer research. Viewers ask questions, compare products and say what they want next. Reading them on the page works for one video. For ten videos, or a competitor's whole channel, you need an export.

Why export YouTube comments

Marketers use comment exports to find content ideas, brands use them to track how a launch lands, and agencies use them to check that an influencer's audience is real. In a spreadsheet, you can sort by likes, filter by keyword and count recurring questions in minutes.

The problem with the YouTube API

The official YouTube Data API can return comments, but you need a Google Cloud project, an API key and code to page through results, and daily quota limits cap how much you can pull. The YouTube Comments Scraper skips all of that: you paste links and get a file.

How to export comments in 4 steps

  1. Copy the links of the videos or Shorts you want. Full links, Shorts links and youtu.be links all work.
  2. Open the YouTube Comments Scraper on Apify and paste up to 20 links into video_urls.
  3. Pick sort_type: Newest for monitoring, Top for the most liked comments. Set max_comments, or turn on scrape_all_comments to get everything.
  4. Press Start, then download the results as Excel, CSV or JSON.
{
  "video_urls": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..."],
  "sort_type": "Top",
  "includeReplies": true,
  "max_comments": 1000
}

Data you get for each comment

GroupFields
Commenttext, likes, publish time, reply count, reply level, isReply
Commentername, channel ID and URL, avatar, verified flag, creator flag
Videotitle, description, keywords, category, duration, publish date, views, likes
Channelchannel name, ID and URL

The creator flag marks replies from the channel owner, which is useful for checking how actively a creator talks to their audience.

5 ways to use comment data

  1. Content ideas: filter for comments containing "how" or "can you" to list the questions your audience asks.
  2. Product feedback: export comments from review videos of your product and your competitors'.
  3. Launch tracking: run the export daily for the first week after a launch video.
  4. Influencer vetting: look for repeated, generic comments that suggest bought engagement.
  5. Sentiment analysis: send the text column to an AI model and score each comment.
faq: How much does it cost?
From $0.50 per 1,000 comments. Exporting 10,000 comments costs about $5.
Does it include replies?
Yes, by default. Set includeReplies to false to collect top-level comments only.
How many videos can I run at once?
Up to 20 links per run. For a whole channel, split the links across several runs or schedule them.

title: How to Scrape Google Maps for Local Business Leads (With Reviews)
desc: Build local B2B lead lists from Google Maps: business names, phones, websites, ratings and reviews by city and category. Step-by-step guide with example inputs.
answer: Open the Google Maps Places & Reviews Scraper on Apify, enter a business type such as "dentist" and a location such as "Austin, TX", set how many places and reviews you want, and run it. Each place comes back with its name, address, phone, website, rating, hours and reviews, ready to export to CSV or your CRM. It starts at $3.00 per 1,000 results.
toc: Why Google Maps is a strong lead source
What you get for each business
How to build a lead list step by step
Four ways to define the search
How to qualify leads with ratings and reviews
body:
Almost every local business has a Google Maps listing, and most keep their phone number, website and opening hours up to date because customers find them there. That makes Google Maps one of the most current lead sources for agencies, SaaS companies and B2B sales teams that sell to local businesses.

Why Google Maps is a strong lead source

  • Coverage: restaurants, clinics, salons, contractors, shops and offices in nearly every city.
  • Freshness: owners update their own listings, so contact details are often more current than bought lists.
  • Built-in qualification: ratings, review counts and claim status tell you how established and active a business is.

What you get for each business

The Google Maps Places & Reviews Scraper returns 44 fields per place, with up to 500 reviews nested inside each one:

GroupFields
Contactname, address, phone, website
Reputationrating, review count, star distribution
Classificationcategories, price range, claim status
Locationcoordinates, Plus Code, timezone
Activityopening hours, popular times
Reviewsrating, text, date, reviewer, owner reply

How to build a lead list step by step

  1. Define your ideal customer. Pick the business type and the cities you sell to, for example dentists in Austin.
  2. Set up the search. Enter "dentist" in searchTerms and "Austin, TX" in locationQuery.
  3. Set the volume. Use maxPlacesPerSearch to control results per search, and maxPlacesTotal to cap the whole run.
  4. Decide on reviews. Set maxReviewsPerPlace to 0 for a contact list only, or 10 to 20 to read what customers say.
  5. Run, export and clean. Export to CSV, remove places without a website or phone, and import the rest into your CRM.
{
  "searchTerms": ["dentist", "orthodontist"],
  "locationQuery": "Austin, TX",
  "maxPlacesPerSearch": 100,
  "maxReviewsPerPlace": 10,
  "language": "en"
}

Four ways to define the search

MethodInputBest for
Keyword and placesearchTerms + locationQueryCity-level lead lists
Map circlelatitude, longitude, radiusKm (up to 500 km)Service areas around a point
Maps linksstartUrlsRe-running a search you built on Google Maps
Place IDsplaceIdsMonitoring known businesses

How to qualify leads with ratings and reviews

Not every listing is a good prospect. Some simple filters help:

  • Unclaimed listings are good leads for local SEO and reputation services.
  • Low ratings with many reviews point to businesses that need help with service or reputation.
  • No website is the clearest signal for web design agencies.
  • Owner replies show an engaged owner who is more likely to respond to outreach.

Using the data responsibly

Business listings are public, but outreach rules still apply. Follow anti-spam and privacy laws in the countries you contact, such as CAN-SPAM in the US and GDPR in the EU, and give people an easy way to opt out. The scraper is an independent tool and is not affiliated with Google.
faq: How much does a lead list cost?
From $3.00 per 1,000 results. A list of 1,000 businesses costs about $3, plus any reviews you choose to include. Check the pricing tab on Apify for current rates.
Does it return email addresses?
No. It returns the phone and website shown on the listing. Many teams then find emails from the website, which we can add in a custom feed.
Can I search in other languages?
Yes. It supports 74 languages through the language setting.

title: Daraz Price Tracking: Monitor Competitor Prices in Bangladesh, Pakistan and More
desc: Set up automated Daraz price tracking across BD, PK, LK, NP and MM. Track competitor prices, discounts and stock daily in Google Sheets, with no code.
answer: Run the Daraz Product Scraper on a daily schedule for your category or competitor search, and send each run to Google Sheets. Every row has a scrapedAt timestamp, so you build a price and discount history for each product automatically. Tracking 1,000 products a day costs about $1 a day.
toc: Set up daily tracking in 4 steps
How to read the price history
When to move to a custom feed
body:
Prices on Daraz change often, especially around campaigns like 11.11 and 12.12. Sellers who react late lose sales, and the search ranking that comes with them. A simple daily price tracker shows you what competitors charge, when they discount and when they run out of stock.

Why track prices on Daraz

  • See competitor price changes the same day, not when your sales drop.
  • Spot discount patterns before big campaigns.
  • Know when a rival goes out of stock, so you can raise visibility while they are gone.
  • Check that resellers keep to your recommended price.

Set up daily tracking in 4 steps

  1. Choose what to track. A category URL covers a whole market segment. A keyword search covers products that compete with yours.
  2. Configure the Daraz Product Scraper. Set the country domain, add your URLs or keywords, and set maxProducts to the number of items you want to watch.
  3. Schedule it. In Apify, create a schedule that runs the scraper every morning.
  4. Send results to Google Sheets. Add the Google Sheets integration so each run appends new rows to the same sheet.

How to read the price history

Each row carries productId, price, originalPrice, discountPct, inStock and scrapedAt. In Google Sheets, a pivot table with products as rows and dates as columns turns this into a price grid. Add conditional formatting to highlight any drop of 10% or more since yesterday.

QuestionFields to use
Who cut their price today?price, scrapedAt
How deep are campaign discounts?originalPrice, discountPct
Who ran out of stock?inStock, sellerName
Which products sell fastest?soldCount over time

Tracking flash sales and campaigns

During campaigns, run the schedule more often, for example every four hours, for the products that matter most. Keep includeOutOfStock on, because sell-outs during a sale are useful demand data.

When to move to a custom feed

A scheduled scraper is enough for most sellers. Teams that track several markets, need product matching across sellers, or want alerts in Slack or email usually move to a custom data feed, where we deliver cleaned, matched data to a database or dashboard and maintain it for them.
faq: How much does daily tracking cost?
At $1.00 per 1,000 products, tracking 1,000 products every day costs about $30 a month.
Can I track all five Daraz countries?
Yes. Run one task per country domain and send them to separate tabs of the same sheet.
Can I get alerts when a price drops?
Apify webhooks can trigger an alert after each run. For ready-made alerts by email or Slack, ask us about a custom feed.
